Because you come here and you think you have an answer for something, and you might have the perfect answer, but you got to convince 218 other people in the house that you're right. And then you got to convince 51 people over in the Senate. Well, the way they're rules are, you got to convince 60 people in the Senate that you're right. Then you got to convince the administration that you're right. And it is a laborious project to get something done. And people will say, well, government shouldn't be that hard to run. I wouldn't want a government that's easy to run. I wouldn't want a government where everybody that has a new idea can just make a law with it and stuff. It ought to go through the rigors of debate and having to convince other members that what you want to do is right. That's okay, but it's frustrating for people out there to go, oh man, you know, why can't Congress ever do anything and that kind of stuff? It's supposed to be hard, and it is. But it is, as I said, the most rewarding job I've ever had being able to represent the people of Idaho.
